mappings.note: Dehydration of ethanol with the role of conc. H2SO4 (LO-8) plus a demand for ethanol's structural formula (C 1.3-LO-4). Both are marked parts, so both are cited; LO-8 leads because the reaction carries most of the marks.

Characteristics of covalent compounds (low melting points, poor conduction, states). This is the chapter's largest gap: no outcome covers the physical properties of covalent compounds, so the competency is cited.
Three reactions of ethanoic acid - with sodium, with NaOH and with ethanol (esterification). All are LO-8 content, so one code covers the item.

Which of C4H8 and C5H12 undergoes addition, and why. The graded point is the reactivity of a multiple bond, which no outcome covers; reading saturation off the general formula (C 1.1-LO-4) is only a sub-step, so it is not cited.
Two unrelated equations: ethanoic acid with sodium carbonate (LO-8) and combustion of methane (no outcome, so C 1.3). Both halves are marked, so both codes are needed.
Both equations involve the two named compounds - burning ethanol and ethanoic acid with NaHCO3 - so a single LO-8 code covers the item, unlike sha 383064977776efd1 where one half is methane.
Why carbon is tetracovalent (it can neither lose nor gain four electrons). The tetravalency clause of LO-3 exactly.

Same molecular formula C3H6O giving an aldehyde and a ketone: structures plus the word 'isomers' is C 1.3-LO-4; naming them propanal and propanone and spotting the two functional groups is C 1.1-LO-4.
Bond formation in CH4 explained from tetravalency - the item names tetravalency itself, so LO-3 rather than the electron-dot outcome C 1.3-LO-4, which would apply if a diagram were demanded.
Observations and equation for ethanoic acid with sodium hydrogencarbonate - a chemical property of ethanoic acid, LO-8.

Identifies ethanol from its sodium reaction (LO-8) and then asks for the name and STRUCTURE of the dehydration product ethene (C 1.3-LO-4). The structure is a separately marked demand, so both codes are cited.

Electron dot structures of F2, NH3 and CCl4. Only CCl4 falls inside C 1.3-LO-4's 'simple carbon compounds'; F2 and NH3 need the bonding competency C 1.1. A clear instance of the outcome's carbon-only wording splitting one item.
Two halves: the position of carbon in the table from its configuration, which only C 1.1 covers, and why carbon forms covalent compounds, which is the tetravalency argument of LO-3.
IUPAC names for an alkyne, an alcohol and a ketone - naming from functional group and chain length, LO-4.
What soaps are chemically and how they differ from detergents - 'distinguishes soaps from detergents' is LO-9 verbatim.
Why unsaturated hydrocarbons undergo addition and saturated ones do not. Addition reactions have no outcome in this frame; C 1.3 competency cited, as for the other reaction-type items.
Detergents in hard water and the change that makes them biodegradable - both sides of the soap-versus-detergent distinction in LO-9.
Electron dot structures of C2H2 and C2H5OH, both carbon compounds, so the outcome applies cleanly here where the F2/NH3 item needed a second code.
Explains the alkyne series with its general formula and first member - homologous series work, LO-4.

Why carbon forms only covalent compounds - the lose/gain-four-electrons argument, which is how LO-3's tetravalency is established. Distinguished from the 'characteristics of covalent compounds' items, which ask about properties and fall to C 1.1.
Medicinal uses of ethanol plus its dehydration to ethene. Both halves concern the named compound, so one LO-8 code.

Why alkanes are called paraffins. Mapped as a question about the alkane homologous series and its general formula (LO-4) rather than to C 1.3, since no reaction is described - only the series' low reactivity as a class trait.

Part (a) defines saponification (LO-8), part (b) contrasts soaps and detergents by composition and hard-water behaviour (LO-9). The item straddles the manufacture/behaviour split deliberately, so both codes are cited.
IUPAC names of a haloalkane and an alkyne, including chain numbering - naming within a homologous series, LO-4.
Physical properties of ethanoic acid (colour, smell, boiling point, miscibility) - 'describes the properties of ... ethanoic acid' is LO-8 word for word.
